object.movement: Hellenistic mosaic (Roman copy after a Hellenistic painting)
object.description: Roman floor mosaic from the House of the Faun at Pompeii, usually dated to about 120–100 BC and thought to copy a lost Hellenistic painting, perhaps by Philoxenus of Eretria. It shows Alexander the Great, bare-headed at the left, charging the Persian king Darius III, who turns in his chariot as his army breaks. Excavated in 1831 and moved to Naples in 1843, it is among the most detailed battle scenes to survive from antiquity. It shows the Battle of Issus, or possibly Gaugamela.
facts: Discovered in 1831 in the House of the Faun, Pompeii, and transferred to Naples in September 1843.
Made of roughly one to one and a half million tesserae about 2 mm wide, laid in curving opus vermiculatum.
The scene depicts more than fifty figures; it is traditionally identified as the Battle of Issus (333 BC).
